A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPHAD research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, visual and tabular benchmark evaluations, ablations, and CSP plant experiments in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark tables, ablations and industrial-use-case evaluation.

M1.justification: The specified evidence computations are corrected: CLIP uses the normal-template numerator instead of the anomalous-template numerator (Section 5.1; Appendix B.3.1), while LOF and Isolation Forest evidence acquire negative signs (Appendix B.3.2). These alter the written score computations while preserving the EPHAD update and adaptive-temperature procedure. The PDFs do not establish changes to the implementation actually used for the experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic example, eight visual datasets, 26 ADBench tabular datasets and simulated CSP plant dataset. No task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments, including the Refine, LOE and SoftPatch comparisons. Changing 'Latent Outlier Factor' to 'Local Outlier Factor' corrects the name of the same cited and evaluated LOF method.

E3.justification: The AUROC metric, splitting and contamination protocols, training settings, and default contamination factor 0.1 and temperature 0.5 remain unchanged. The evidence-formula corrections do not introduce a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The synthetic illustration and analyses of contamination, temperature and test-set anomaly proportion are unchanged, including Figures 1–5, Section 5.3 and Appendices C.4–C.5.

E5.justification: Standard-error reporting in the result tables and the three-seed repetition statement in Appendix C.1 are identical. No uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–2 and 4–10 and Figures 1–5. The corrected evidence formulas are not accompanied by revised result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of the CLIP, LOF and Isolation Forest evidence functions change their orientation to favor normal samples. These are non-equivalent formula corrections. Proposition 4.1, its proof in Appendix A.1, and the remaining assumptions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about post-hoc adaptation without training access, flexible evidence sources and effectiveness across anomaly-detection settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning weak evidence, sensitivity to temperature, and limitations of the adaptive variant remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same discussion of uncalibrated inlier probabilities, domain-specific evidence and future work.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects the explicit instructions for computing evidence through the CLIP numerator change and LOF/Isolation Forest sign changes. Other reproducibility information, including prompts, preprocessing, training hyperparameters, A100/CPU usage and code-access links, is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The LOF terminology correction retains the same Breunig et al. citation and does not introduce a different prior method.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction correct 'Latent Outlier Factor' to 'Local Outlier Factor', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Section organization and the surrounding narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10 retain their design, captions, structure and placement. No figure or table is added, removed, redrawn or reorganized, and the page layout is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects evidence formulas that conflicted with Section 4's requirement that higher evidence values favor normal samples. The CLIP numerator correction and negative LOF/Isolation Forest scores improve consistency and the reliability of implementation from the paper. This is a focused improvement; the empirical support, theoretical guarantees and stated limitations remain unchanged.
